facts.fact: The project's authors state that a clinical information system built on MediBoard was deployed for outpatient consultations in the gynaecology-obstetrics department of Yaoundé Central Hospital, a national referral hospital, and after six months counted 113 users, 1,278 patient records and 960 consultations; staff then stopped entering data when the per-entry payment ended and the second part never ran. The article dates none of this, so its published date is used.

The authors state that data were entered on computers in consultation rooms, doctors' offices and treatment rooms and held on a server at the hospital reached over its own intranet, with paper service registers kept in parallel and senior gynaecologists passing their logins to residents and students to enter records for them; no date is given, so the published date is used.

The authors state that the system ran under a cooperation agreement between Yaoundé Central Hospital, the data owner, and Geneva University Hospitals, backed only by the hospital's director, with the government not directly involved; no date is given, so the published date is used.

The authors state that of a CHF 60,000 budget the project received CHF 40,000 from Geneva University Hospitals, and that the CHF 20,000 third owed by Yaoundé Central Hospital was not paid; no date is given, so the published date is used.

systems.platform: MediBoard (open source), with a locally developed billing and cash management module
systems.owner: Yaoundé Central Hospital, with Geneva University Hospitals
systems.tiers: outpatient consultations of the gynaecology-obstetrics department of Yaoundé Central Hospital, a national referral hospital; one pilot unit

note: The article gives no dates for the project. It also states that Cameroon had no national digital health strategy when the project ran, that one was adopted in January 2020, and that an operational plan under it was being designed; these are not tied to a dated fact about the system.
